title: GenWave Persona Catalog Index
description: The committed index.json shape (SPEC F89.2) a GenWave station fetches directly from the repo root — built from entries/ by tools/build_index.py, and re-verified byte-for-byte plus schema-validated on every CI run (PR and push to main). additionalProperties is false throughout: this document is entirely catalog-tooling output, so an unrecognized field is a build regression worth failing CI on, not a forward-compat concern.
$comment: Every pattern below ends in (?![\s\S]), a lookahead meaning 'no character follows' — a portable absolute-end-of-string anchor that means the same thing in Python re, ECMA-262 (the dialect JSON Schema nominally specifies, and what ajv/most other validators use), and .NET. Plain $ was rejected: in Python's re (which is what actually enforces this schema server-side, via the jsonschema library), $ also matches immediately before a trailing newline, so a value with a stray trailing \n would slip through. \Z was also tried and rejected: it's Python-only — under ECMA-262, \Z is a literal 'Z' character (Annex B identity escape), so a \Z-anchored pattern would reject every legitimate value and only accept ones ending in a literal Z. (?![\s\S]) has neither problem in any of the three dialects.

generatedAt.description: ISO 8601 date (YYYY-MM-DD): the max `added` date across included entries' meta.json, or 1970-01-01 when the catalog has zero included entries (tools/build_index.py). Derived entirely from the tree, never from git history or wall-clock time.

entries.description: Sorted by slug. Never includes the example-dj documentation entry.

swatchSet.description: The five shelf-chip swatches for one mode (mirrors schemas/theme-meta.schema.json's own `swatchSet`).

assetRef.description: One binary asset carried by a kind:"font" entry's `assets[]` (SPEC F104.1) — a latin-subsetted woff2 face or the pack's OFL licence text, sitting alongside (never inside) its `<slug>.font.json` manifest. Mirrors GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator's own asset-ref shape: closed extension set (woff2|txt), bare-filename character set (no further path segment possible), and a positive byte count bounded by the app's own fetch-transport size cap.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out. UNLIKE the manifest/meta path patterns above (whose filename segment must equal the slug), an asset's filename is the pack's OWN file name (e.g. "space-grotesk-variable-latin.woff2", "OFL.txt") — this pattern constrains character set and extension only, the same closed set (woff2|txt) GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.AssetFileNameText enforces app-side.

bytes.description: Declared byte size of this asset. Bounded 1-262144 (256 KiB) — the SAME per-asset ceiling GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogProxyService.MaxAssetBytes enforces at fetch time; an asset declaring more than the app will ever accept is malformed by definition, so this schema is at least as strict as the app rather than deferring the rejection to fetch time.

entry.description: `card`/`manifest` (and, for kind:"font", `assets`) are conditionally required, not all listed here — see the `if`/`then`/`else` below, gated on `kind`.

kind.description: Entry discriminator (SPEC F103.2 / T178, widened to "font" by F104.1 / T195). Optional — an entry with no `kind` is treated as "persona", matching every pre-F103.2 entry and the app's own back-compat default (GenWave.Host, T176: a missing `kind` defaults to persona; an unrecognized `kind` value there causes the app to skip just that one entry, not abort the whole index — this schema is stricter than the app and rejects an unrecognized value outright, since here it can only mean a build regression in this repo's own tooling, not a newer app talking to an older catalog). `kind` decides which file-ref property below is required and which path pattern its `path` must match: "persona" (or omitted) requires `card` matching `*.persona.json` — the unchanged, pre-F103.2 shape; "theme" requires `manifest` matching `*.theme.json`; "font" requires BOTH `manifest` matching `*.font.json` AND a non-empty `assets` array (SPEC F104.1 — a font entry is `{manifest, meta}` plus its vendored asset files, the first binary files in the catalog).

preview.description: Projected from a kind:"theme" entry's meta.json (T191, mirrors the `bestFor` precedent above) — the shelf-card swatch contract (T185): a HANDFUL of key token hex values per mode, enough to paint shelf chips without fetching and parsing the full manifest. Only ever present on a kind:"theme" entry; a persona entry's meta.json carries no `preview` field, so build_index.py never stamps this key onto one. Excluded from a kind:"font" entry too (T195 review N8) — the font `then` branch's own `allOf` rejects a font entry carrying this key, the same posture the theme branch already takes on `assets`/`family`: a font pack has no swatch preview to project, T191's projection is theme-only. Definitions duplicated from schemas/theme-meta.schema.json rather than $ref'd across files, the same standalone-file posture that schema's own $comment documents for its `added` pattern.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out.

Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ to the kind:"theme" or kind:"font" manifest file (SPEC F103.2 / F104.1) — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out. The exact required extension (`*.theme.json` for a theme entry, `*.font.json` for a font entry) is deliberately NOT enforced here — it's pinned per-kind by the `manifest.path` pattern nested in each `if`/`then`/`else` branch below instead, so a theme entry naming a `.font.json` manifest (or vice versa) fails there rather than validating against this shared, kind-blind definition (a prior version of this pattern accepted either extension regardless of `kind`, letting the two cross-dress). The one `manifest` key every non-persona kind targets (F103.2's generalised `{manifest, meta}` model); persona entries keep using `card` (see the `kind` description above) rather than this key — and, as of the persona `else` branch's own `allOf` (T195 review N7), are schema-rejected from carrying this key at all: an entry with no `kind` (or `kind: "persona"`) that names both `card` and `manifest` validated clean before that addition even though it's a shape GenWave.Host's own kind resolution never produces and would reject the whole index over app-side (exactly one of `card`/`manifest` is ever expected, never both).

assets.description: A kind:"font" entry's vendored asset files (SPEC F104.1) — 1-2 latin-subsetted woff2 faces plus the pack's OFL licence text, each carrying `path`/`sha256`/`bytes`. Only ever present on a kind:"font" entry; persona/theme entries carry no `assets` key. minItems 1 mirrors GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator's own "zero assets" rejection (TryValidateAssets) — this schema is at least as strict, rejecting an empty array at CI time rather than only at app fetch time. uniqueItems (T196) is full-object uniqueness (path/sha256/bytes all equal, not just a duplicate `path`) — a font entry's own assets[] should never carry the same asset twice, the same posture files[]'s own duplicate-asset gate already takes one layer down in the pack's own manifest (tools/validate.py's font-duplicate-asset check). Because draft-07 has no way to pin uniqueness on a single property alone, uniqueItems does NOT by itself catch two assets sharing the same `path` with a DIFFERENT `sha256`/`bytes` — the app dedupes an entry's assets on `path` ALONE (CatalogIndexValidator.TryValidateAssets again), so that pair would silently lose one asset app-side even though it passes this schema untouched. tools/validate.py's validate_index_duplicate_asset_paths (T196 review M2) is the actual gate against that case, the same Python-side cross-property posture validate_index_slug_ownership already takes for path ownership.

family.description: The OPTIONAL shelf-card family name projected onto a kind:"font" entry (STORY-281 AC1, T195/T196 — copied from the pack's own manifest `family` by tools/build_index.py so a zero-fetch shelf listing can show it without fetching `.font.json`). Shape and length mirror GenWave.Host.Catalog.CatalogIndexValidator.FamilyPattern/MaxFamilyLength exactly — the same CSS-injection-safe character set (and 64-character cap) ThemeManifestParser.FontFamilyPattern enforces on a theme manifest's own font family, since this value reaches the wire (and an inline CSS `style`/`font-family` value) the same way a theme's shelf preview swatches do.

path.description: Repo-root-relative POSIX path under entries/<slug>/ — no leading slash, no .., no URL scheme; the pattern's own shape rules all three out.
